messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you sell your acoustic guitar quickly and safely: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |------|------------|----------------|------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body). Tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑presented instrument looks more valuable and shows you care. | Use a quality cleaning kit; replace old strings if they’re worn. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the whole instrument from multiple angles (front, back, sides, headstock, bridge, sound hole). Include close‑ups of any scratches, dents, or repairs. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce questions. | Use natural light, a plain background, and a decent camera or smartphone. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music stores. Note price ranges for similar models, ages, and conditions. | Knowing the market helps you set a realistic price and avoid over‑ or under‑pricing. | Look at “completed listings” on eBay to see what actually sold for. | | **4. Write a Detailed Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, wood type, finish, any modifications, and condition notes. Mention any accessories (case, strap, picks). | Transparency builds trust and reduces returns. | Use bullet points for clarity; keep the tone friendly but factual. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, buyer protection.
• **eBay** – large audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local music shops** – consignment or direct sale. | Different platforms reach different buyers. | If you’re comfortable shipping, Reverb or eBay gives buyer protection. For local sales, Craigslist/Facebook is faster. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point can still land you a good deal. | Consider adding a “price‑match” clause if you’re selling locally. | | **7. Decide on Shipping or Pickup** | • **Local pickup** – no shipping cost, instant payment.
• **Shipping** – use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and insured freight. | Shipping expands your buyer pool but adds cost and risk. | Offer free shipping if you can absorb the cost; otherwise, factor it into the price. | | **8. Secure Payment** | • **Cash** – safest for local sales.
• **PayPal / Venmo** – secure for online sales.
• **Escrow** – Reverb’s built‑in protection. | Protects against fraud and ensures you get paid. | Never accept personal checks or wire transfers unless you’re sure of the buyer. | | **9. Handle Negotiations Professionally** | Respond promptly, keep tone polite, and be prepared to justify your price. | Good communication can close the deal faster. | Have a minimum acceptable price in mind before you start negotiating. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | Once payment is confirmed, ship or hand over the guitar. Provide a receipt or confirmation email. | Documentation protects both parties. | Keep a copy of the transaction details for your records. | ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Clean & tune guitar - [ ] Take 8–10 high‑quality photos - [ ] Research comparable listings - [ ] Draft a clear, honest description - [ ] List on 1–2 platforms (Reverb + local marketplace) - [ ] Set a realistic starting price - [ ] Decide on shipping vs. pickup - [ ] Secure payment method - [ ] Negotiate politely - [ ] Ship/hand over with receipt ### Extra Tips - **Appraisal**: If you’re unsure of value, get a quick appraisal from a local shop or an online service. - **Consignment**: Some shops will sell on your behalf for a commission—good if you don’t want to handle the sale yourself. - **Safety**: For local pickups, meet in a public place or a store’s customer area. - **Return Policy**: If you’re shipping, consider a short return window (e.g., 3–5 days) to build buyer confidence. By following these steps, you’ll present your guitar professionally, attract serious buyers, and close the sale with confidence. Good luck!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "How can I sell my acoustic guitar?" They want advice. We can provide steps: research market value, clean instrument, take photos, list on platforms (eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, Reverb, local classifieds), set price, describe condition, shipping options, safety tips. Also mention potential appraisal, trade-in, consignment. Provide tips for negotiation, payment methods, etc. No function call needed.
